normalized.prelim_summary: This 2008 BMW Z4 3.0si roadster is a desirable manual 6-speed example with a clean AutoCheck history and no accidents, but the seller discloses a torn top, an active ABS light, and worn trim rubber. At $14,700 with 47,722 miles, buyers should budget for the top repair and brake system diagnosis.

ppi_focus: Full DSC/ABS diagnostic with a BMW-capable scanner: wheel-speed sensors, DSC module/pump, brake fluid level and moisture content, pad wear sensors
Base brake function and pedal feel with ABS/EBD disabled; road test for pulling or lockup
Cooling system: pressure test, inspect the 2025 radiator install, electric water pump and thermostat codes and performance, coolant temperature in traffic
Soft top: tear extent, top hydraulics and pump, drain channels, trunk floor, battery well and footwell moisture, corrosion at connectors and modules
Behind the front bumper cover: bumper reinforcement, radiator support, AC condenser, crash-bar mounts for collision damage
N52 oil leaks: oil filter housing gasket, valve cover gasket, oil pan; eccentric-shaft sensor and VANOS codes; cold-start lifter tick
EPS: on-center notchiness, assist consistency, stored steering faults
Front control-arm bushings, ball joints, rear shocks and mounts; tire date codes and wear pattern
Clutch engagement, slave cylinder, shifter bushings
Powertrain readiness monitors and pending codes ahead of CA smog
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the ABS/BRAKE fault is diagnosed as a wheel-speed sensor or similarly minor fix with a written quote, and the trunk and battery well are dry.
Up: invoices show the 2025 radiator job was preventive, a water pump/thermostat receipt surfaces, and the seller prices in the top and bumper work.
Down: a failed DSC module, a brake hydraulic fault, or evidence of an overheat behind the 2025 radiator replacement.
Down: water intrusion with corroded modules or wiring, or hidden damage behind the front bumper cover.
evidence.mission_note: A 3.0si six-speed roadster in the ideal price band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief on spec. As listed, it carries an active brake-system warning and a torn top, so it serves as a bridge only after diagnosis and repair rather than on arrival.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode and attached CARFAX establish a 2008 Z4 3.0si six-speed with a guaranteed clean title, three California owners (the current one for about 15 years), a consistent odometer chain near 47.5k mi, and mostly BMW-dealer servicing. CARFAX also documents a radiator and coolant reservoir replacement in 06/2025 and a coolant flush in 04/2024. The listing and photos establish real faults: ABS and red BRAKE warning lights lit, a torn soft top, and a cracked lower front bumper at both corners. The bumper damage appears in neither history report, while CARFAX separately records 2020 roof damage that AutoCheck omits. The dash photo shows 46,631 mi, matching the 04/2025 CARFAX reading, so the photos may be about a year old, and the warning lights appear to have been on since then. Open items are the cause of the brake/DSC fault, any water intrusion through the top, the N52 electric water pump and thermostat (no reported entry), brake fluid (no reported flush since 2011), PCV heater recall completion, and the condition behind the bumper. The $14,700 asking sits inside the $14,075–$15,825 fair-value band, but known work is substantial relative to it.
evidence.next_action: Send the seller the question list, prioritising the DSC/ABS fault-code scan, trunk floor and battery-well photos, the 06/2025 radiator invoice, and agreement to an independent BMW PPI near the car before any deposit.
